Case Study
-
This is a case study. Case studies are not timed separately. You can use as much exam time as you would like to complete each case. However, there may be additional case studies and sections on this exam. You must manage your time to ensure that you are able to complete all questions included on this exam in the time provided.
To answer the questions included in a case study, you will need to reference information that is provided in the case study. Case studies might contain exhibits and other resources that provide more information about the scenario that is described in the case study. Each question is independent of the other questions in this case study.
At the end of this case study, a review screen will appear. This screen allows you to review your answers and to make changes before you move to the next section of the exam. After you begin a new section, you cannot return to this section.
To start the case study
-
To display the first question in this case study, click the Next button. Use the buttons in the left pane to explore the content of the case study before you answer the questions. Clicking these buttons displays information such as business requirements, existing environment, and problem statements. When you are ready to answer a question, click the Question button to return to the question.
Background
-
Proseware, Inc. is an industry leading software company with several thousand employees. The company has had some trouble recruiting talented employees. Top-level candidates interview with the company but go on to work for competitors.
Feedback from candidates show that some offers were not accepted because the interview scheduling process was unpleasant. The company does not have a system to keep track of the candidates that were not selected.
Current Environment
-
The recruiting process starts when an individual applies for a position on the company website. The individual may have found the position on their own, they may have been officially referred by an employee, or in some cases were contacted directly by a hiring manager and encouraged to apply.
Recruiters schedule an interview with a hiring manager and interviews with two senior team members. Each interview results in feedback about the candidate and a recommendation whether to hire or not.
The recruiting team manages all information by using a model-driven application.
The company has the following Microsoft Dataverse tables and columns:
• JobPosting
- Hiring Manager - lookup to SystemUser
- Recruiter Assigned - lookup to SystemUser
• Contact (Job Applicant)
- Contact identifier
- First name
- Last name
- Time-Zone Offset
- Person of Interest - Yes/No (default)
• Application proapplication
- Contact identifier, Contact - lookup to Contact
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
- pro_recruiterassignedid
• Interview
- Application - lookup to Application
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
- Recommend - Choice (Yes (0), No (1), and null (default) are the available values)
- Person of Interest - Yes/No, No is the default value
• Referral
- Contact - lookup to Contact
- Referrer - lookup to SystemUser
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
• SystemUser
- Manager - lookup to SystemUser
- Time-Zone Offset
• Recruiter
- Recruiter identifier
- Recruiter name
Applications
-
There may be multiple applications associated with each job posting. Applications are linked to an employee record if an employee referred the applicant for a position. The same individual can be an applicant for multiple job postings.
Interviews
-
Each interview is performed by an employee and is related to a single application.
The interview scheduling process may force potential candidates to accept interviews at unusual times with the senior team members due to time-zone differences.
Requirements. Interview Scheduling
The system must provide recruiters with a list of team members and their time-zone information. You must create a Microsoft Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) control for the Job Application form to display a list of senior team members who report directly to a hiring manager.
• The control must display the current time in each team member's local time.
• The control must be bound so that it minimizes the amount of code that must be written.
• You must display the list of team members and sort the list to show team members who reside in time zones closest to the applicant's time zone first.
You must develop a second PCF control that displays the time-zone name and current time on the Job Application form. You must display the data in the candidate’s local time.
Requirements. Historical Information Tracking
You must create a process to identify individuals as a person of interest that the company should consider hiring. You must assign each individual a score based on their past interactions.
• You must be able to determine the following information about a candidate:
- The number of interviews in the past two years and whether team members provided recommendations
- The number of hiring manager referrals and employee referrals in the past two years
- Whether the individual has any of the 12 designations or certifications that the company considers significant
• Only a single referral can be made per job application. The system must be able to support multiple referrals for a candidate.
• The system must track referrals even if an application is not completed.
Requirements. Historical Information Scoring
The automated process must run weekly to assess all candidates. The process must also run automatically when historical information is updated. You must be able to perform scoring by selecting a command button on the contact form.
• This new command button must only be visible to employees who belong to a security role assigned named Recruiter. The command button must not be visible to anyone unless the contact form is in Update mode.
• A person of interest is defined as having a score of 15 or more based on the following historical information criteria:
- Each interview with a recommendation adds two to the score.
- Each interview without a recommendation subtracts two from the score.
- Each employee or manager referral adds one to the score.
- Each designation or certification adds one to the score.
• All scoring elements must be recalculated when changes occur. You must assign the score to the Person of interest field.
• Values representing totals or scores must be stored in their own numeric fields.
• Plug-ins must be used to keep the Person of Interest field on active interview records associated with the Contact.
• Plug-ins registered on the update of the Person of interest field must send an email notification when the candidate named in the email is a person of interest. Recruiters must receive the message when the field is updated on the Contact record.
• Interviewers must get an email notification when the Person of Interest field on the interview record is successfully updated.
Requirements. Design Guidelines
The following design guidelines must be followed:
• Schema changes must be made using the method requiring the least amount of storage to meet the requirement.
• Out-of-the-box functionality must be used when possible.
• Any code required to calculate scores must be able to be run from a single point.
• Email notifications need to be kept to a minimum.
Issues
-
• Recruiters report that the command button to score a candidate is not working. You debug the code and observe that the context input parameter is null.
• The system does not support associating designations and certifications with candidates.
• The value for the field used by the PCF control to display local time is saved to Microsoft Dataverse each time an active application record is opened.
• Interviewers report that they do not receive email notifications when interview records are created for an existing person of interest.
You need to configure the columns to store scores and totals.
Which configurations should you use? To answer, drag the appropriate configurations to the correct columns. Each configuration may be used once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to drag the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

Background
-
Proseware, Inc. is an industry leading software company with several thousand employees. The company has had some trouble recruiting talented employees. Top-level candidates interview with the company but go on to work for competitors.
Feedback from candidates show that some offers were not accepted because the interview scheduling process was unpleasant. The company does not have a system to keep track of the candidates that were not selected.
Current Environment
-
The recruiting process starts when an individual applies for a position on the company website. The individual may have found the position on their own, they may have been officially referred by an employee, or in some cases were contacted directly by a hiring manager and encouraged to apply.
Recruiters schedule an interview with a hiring manager and interviews with two senior team members. Each interview results in feedback about the candidate and a recommendation whether to hire or not.
The recruiting team manages all information by using a model-driven application.
The company has the following Microsoft Dataverse tables and columns:
• JobPosting
- Hiring Manager - lookup to SystemUser
- Recruiter Assigned - lookup to SystemUser
• Contact (Job Applicant)
- Contact identifier
- First name
- Last name
- Time-Zone Offset
- Person of Interest - Yes/No (default)
• Application proapplication
- Contact identifier, Contact - lookup to Contact
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
- pro_recruiterassignedid
• Interview
- Application - lookup to Application
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
- Recommend - Choice (Yes (0), No (1), and null (default) are the available values)
- Person of Interest - Yes/No, No is the default value
• Referral
- Contact - lookup to Contact
- Referrer - lookup to SystemUser
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
• SystemUser
- Manager - lookup to SystemUser
- Time-Zone Offset
• Recruiter
- Recruiter identifier
- Recruiter name
Applications
-
There may be multiple applications associated with each job posting. Applications are linked to an employee record if an employee referred the applicant for a position. The same individual can be an applicant for multiple job postings.
Interviews
-
Each interview is performed by an employee and is related to a single application.
The interview scheduling process may force potential candidates to accept interviews at unusual times with the senior team members due to time-zone differences.
Requirements. Interview Scheduling
The system must provide recruiters with a list of team members and their time-zone information. You must create a Microsoft Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) control for the Job Application form to display a list of senior team members who report directly to a hiring manager.
• The control must display the current time in each team member's local time.
• The control must be bound so that it minimizes the amount of code that must be written.
• You must display the list of team members and sort the list to show team members who reside in time zones closest to the applicant's time zone first.
You must develop a second PCF control that displays the time-zone name and current time on the Job Application form. You must display the data in the candidate’s local time.
Requirements. Historical Information Tracking
You must create a process to identify individuals as a person of interest that the company should consider hiring. You must assign each individual a score based on their past interactions.
• You must be able to determine the following information about a candidate:
- The number of interviews in the past two years and whether team members provided recommendations
- The number of hiring manager referrals and employee referrals in the past two years
- Whether the individual has any of the 12 designations or certifications that the company considers significant
• Only a single referral can be made per job application. The system must be able to support multiple referrals for a candidate.
• The system must track referrals even if an application is not completed.
Requirements. Historical Information Scoring
The automated process must run weekly to assess all candidates. The process must also run automatically when historical information is updated. You must be able to perform scoring by selecting a command button on the contact form.
• This new command button must only be visible to employees who belong to a security role assigned named Recruiter. The command button must not be visible to anyone unless the contact form is in Update mode.
• A person of interest is defined as having a score of 15 or more based on the following historical information criteria:
- Each interview with a recommendation adds two to the score.
- Each interview without a recommendation subtracts two from the score.
- Each employee or manager referral adds one to the score.
- Each designation or certification adds one to the score.
• All scoring elements must be recalculated when changes occur. You must assign the score to the Person of interest field.
• Values representing totals or scores must be stored in their own numeric fields.
• Plug-ins must be used to keep the Person of Interest field on active interview records associated with the Contact.
• Plug-ins registered on the update of the Person of interest field must send an email notification when the candidate named in the email is a person of interest. Recruiters must receive the message when the field is updated on the Contact record.
• Interviewers must get an email notification when the Person of Interest field on the interview record is successfully updated.
Requirements. Design Guidelines
The following design guidelines must be followed:
• Schema changes must be made using the method requiring the least amount of storage to meet the requirement.
• Out-of-the-box functionality must be used when possible.
• Any code required to calculate scores must be able to be run from a single point.
• Email notifications need to be kept to a minimum.
Issues

• The system does not support associating designations and certifications with candidates.
• The value for the field used by the PCF control to display local time is saved to Microsoft Dataverse each time an active application record is opened.
• Interviewers report that they do not receive email notifications when interview records are created for an existing person of interest.

questions.examQue:
A company uses a plug-in within Dataverse to perform complex calculations of data in near real time.
The calculations often run longer than five minutes, which causes the plug-in to time out.
You need to recommend an appropriate replacement component.
What should you recommend?

  • A. Azure Event Hub
  • B. Azure Data Factory
  • C. Azure Functions
  • D. Azure Databricks
questions.examAnsDesc:
Justification

  • Azure Functions (C) – Correct choice

    • Serverless compute that can execute long‑running tasks (up to 10 minutes on the Consumption plan, or unlimited with Premium/App Service plan).
    • Automatically scales, integrates with Dataverse triggers, and avoids the 5‑minute plug‑in timeout.
    • Supports C#, JavaScript, Python, etc., allowing the same complex calculation logic to be reused with minimal code changes.

  • Azure Event Hub (A) – Not suitable

    • Designed for high‑throughput event ingestion and streaming, not for executing custom business logic.
    • Does not provide a runtime environment for calculations; it only transports data.

  • Azure Data Factory (B) – Not suitable

    • Primarily an orchestration service for data movement and transformation pipelines (ETL).
    • While it can run data flows, it is over‑engineered for simple plug‑in replacement and lacks direct, low‑latency invocation from Dataverse.

  • Azure Databricks (D) – Not suitable

    • A managed Spark cluster geared toward big‑data analytics and machine‑learning workloads.
    • Introduces heavy infrastructure overhead and longer provisioning times, making it impractical for near‑real‑time, short‑lived calculations that previously ran in a plug‑in.

Conclusion: Azure Functions best replaces the timed‑out plug‑in by offering a lightweight, scalable, and near‑real‑time execution environment that fits the existing calculation logic and avoids the 5‑minute timeout constraint.

You are writing C# code to create an alternate key in a table for two columns: Order ID and Order Date. The table has thousands of records.
You use the CreateEntityKey message to create the key. When you retrieve EntityKeyMetadata.EntityKeyIndexStatus, it returns a value of Failed.
You need to resolve the issue with the index creation.
What should you do first?

  • A. Use the ReactivateEntityKey action.
  • B. Publish customizations.
  • C. Use the DeleteEntityKeyRequest message.
  • D. Delete duplicate combination values in Order ID and Order Date.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Justification

  • Correct option – A. Use the ReactivateEntityKey action

    • The CreateEntityKey message fails with EntityKeyIndexStatus.Failed when the underlying index cannot be created because duplicate values already exist in the key columns.
    • ReactivateEntityKey forces the platform to re‑evaluate the key definition, clears the failed status, and allows the system to enforce the alternate key after any duplicate rows have been resolved (or after a successful publish).
    • This is the first step recommended by the Power Apps/ Power Automate documentation: reactivate the key to reset its state before attempting any further remediation.

  • Why the other options are not appropriate as the first step

    • B. Publish customizations – Publishing merely makes pending changes visible to the environment; it does not resolve a failed key‑creation status caused by duplicate data.
    • C. DeleteEntityKeyRequest – Deleting the key would remove the definition entirely, requiring you to recreate it later; it does not address the underlying duplicate‑value condition that caused the failure.
    • D. Delete duplicate combination values in Order ID and Order Date – While removing duplicates is necessary for a successful key creation, it is an operational data‑cleanup step, not the initial action the platform expects when the key’s status is “Failed.” The proper first step is to reactivate the key so the system can re‑evaluate the definition after cleanup.

Conclusion
The immediate remediation for a failed EntityKeyIndexStatus is to invoke the ReactivateEntityKey action, which resets the key’s state and prepares the system for subsequent validation or publication. This aligns with the platform’s prescribed workflow for handling alternate key creation errors.

A model-driven app form has JavaScript that runs during the OnLoad event. The event retrieves an account record and changes visibility to a form column based on one of the record columns. The following portion of code retrieves the account record:
Xrm.WebApi.retrieveRecord('account', accountId)_
Users report that the form loads slowly.
You need to improve the performance of the code that retrieves the account and changes visibility.
What should you do?

  • A. Use a synchronous XMLHttpRequest instead.
  • B. Add the code to change visibility to the success callback.
  • C. Enable the Async OnLoad app setting.
  • D. Set the options parameter to return only the column required.
  • E. Store the returned data in a global variable.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Technical justification

  • The form’s OnLoad script currently uses Xrm.WebApi.retrieveRecord without any configuration to limit the payload or to run asynchronously.
  • Enabling the Async OnLoad app setting tells the platform to execute the OnLoad script in an asynchronous context, allowing the UI to render first and then fetch the account record in the background. This eliminates the blocking call that is causing the perceived slowness.
  • The asynchronous pattern also lets you place the visibility‑change logic in the success callback, ensuring it runs only after the data is actually retrieved, but the key performance gain comes from the async execution mode itself.
  • Why the other options are inferior
    • A – Synchronous XMLHttpRequest – Would block the UI thread, making the form appear even slower and violating best‑practice performance guidelines.
    • B – Add the code to the success callback – While this is a good practice, it does not address the root cause (synchronous execution) and therefore does not improve load time on its own.
    • D – Return only the required column – Reducing the attribute list can shave a few milliseconds, but the dominant delay is the synchronous call; without async execution the UI still waits for the round‑trip.
    • E – Store the returned data in a global variable – Caching data does not reduce the initial network latency; it only helps subsequent calls, not the first load.

Conclusion – Enabling the Async OnLoad app setting is the most direct way to improve performance because it removes the blocking nature of the OnLoad script, allowing the UI to become interactive sooner while the record is fetched in the background.

References

  • Model‑driven apps – Form scripts and events (Async execution)
  • Xrm.WebApi.retrieveRecord – Retrieve only needed attributes

A company uses Microsoft Dataverse rollup fields to calculate insurance exposure and risk profiles for customers.
Users report that the system does not update values for the rollup fields when new insurance policies are written.
You need to recalculate the value of the rollup fields immediately after a policy is created.
What should you do?
  • A. Create new fields on the customer entity for insurance exposure and risk. Write a workflow process that is triggered when a new policy record is created to calculate the sum of values from policy records.
  • B. Update the Mass Calculate Rollup Field job to trigger when a new policy record is created.
  • C. Create a plug-in that uses the update method for the rollup fields. Configure a step on the Create event for the policy entity for this plug-in.
  • D. Create a plug-in that uses the CalculateRollupFieldRequest method for the rollup field. Configure a step on the Create event for the policy entity for this plug-in.
questions.examAnsDesc:
D. Create a plug-in that uses the CalculateRollupFieldRequest method for the rollup field. Configure a step on the Create event for the policy entity for this plug-in.

Option A is not correct because it would require additional fields and workflows which would make the solution complex.

Option B is not correct because Mass Calculate Rollup Field job runs periodically and it wouldn't update immediately after the policy is created.

Option C is not correct because the update method is used to update the values of an existing record and it wouldn't recalculate the value of the rollup field.

Background
-
City Power & Light is an energy and utilities company that has offices in Europe. The company subsidizes home improvements for domestic customers, to improve energy efficiency and to meet environmental commitments. The company also distributes and generates electricity for domestic and commercial customers. The company has 2,000 employees in multiple offices and in work-from-home locations.
City Power & Light uses a team of schedulers, assessors, field engineers, and customer support agents for home improvements in a program named Get Energy Fit.
Current Environment
-
Get Energy Fit Program
-
City Power & Light uses the following to manage the Get Energy Fit program:
•The company uses a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet named Planning Hub on Microsoft SharePoint Online to store information about customer appointments, customer details, and customer eligibility in the program.
•The company records sensitive customer information that includes the document identification numbers and the customer's financial information.
•The company uses an assessor to verify customer eligibility in the program and to perform a suitability assessment. The assessor completes the suitability assessment by using a paper and clipboard at the customer property and enters the data to the Planning Hub after the assessment is completed. The assessor also uploads photographs to an on-premises document library. The assessor completes the eligibility assessment by using an application written in React.
•Schedulers use Microsoft Outlook to schedule engineers and assessors for home improvement appointments. About 200 appointments are scheduled daily.
•Employees for the company submit funding claims on behalf of the customer by uploading evidence and compliance checks information to an application named the Claim Submission Portal.
Technical Environment
-
•Schedulers use Windows 11 desktop and laptop computers with the latest version of Microsoft Edge.
•Assessors use iOS and Android tablet devices.
•The Claim Submission Portal uses REST-based APIs for all operations and a dedicated testing environment. Authentication to the API is provided by using the following example header key and value pair:
oAuthentication: 2C8D41431415E429C7FC7A74D8315
•The company uses Microsoft Azure for hosting multiple applications.
Requirements
-
Overview
-
City Power & Light plans to implement Microsoft Power Platform to improve the customer experience and increase delivery for the Get Energy Fit program.
Business Requirements
-
•Only team leaders and senior managers should have access to read personally identifiable information (PII).
•All development changes must be tested in a separate environment.
•The company requires out-of-the-box solutions, when possible.
•Sensitive credentials, such as user passwords and API secrets, must be stored securely.
•The Claim Submission Portal must allow citizen developers to create automated solutions.
•Customer and appointment information must be accessible to all applications.
Planning Hub Application
-
The company is planning to replace the Planning Hub spreadsheet with a new application. The new application has the following requirements:
•The application must support a component design that provides rapid changes requested by the schedulers.
•The data model for the application must capture the following information:
oInformation about customers such as name, address, and other PII.
oThe data and time for an assessor's or engineer's appointment. Schedulers must be able to view all appointments without filters.
oRecords the details of the home improvements installed for the customer.
oContains all the information and evidence for submission to the Claim Submission Portal.
•After an assessor uploads the funding application and all evidence after a home improvement has been complete, the company requires that the status of the application is set to Submit and should run the following:
oRetrieve the details about the customer and the improvement installed.
oSend an approval to a senior manager to review and approve in Microsoft Teams.
oUpload the information to the API endpoint.
oIf the upload fails to complete, it should retry after a delay of 30 seconds up to three times. If an error occurs after three times, the application should send an email notification to the application support team.
oMust record the status on the funding application.
Suitability Assessment Tool
-
The company plans to implement a new application named the Suitability Assessment Tool for the assessors. The new application has the following requirements:
•Must integrate with Microsoft Power Platform.
•Assessors must be able to complete the eligibility assessment by using the Suitability Assessment Tool. The assessors must be able to upload photographs to the on-premises file share.
•Must be developed by using modular components that can be used by other applications.
•Must be optimized for use on tablet devices.
•All changes to the application must be completed in the Suitability Assessment Tool solution.
Reporting
-
The company has the following requirements for a reporting solution:
•The data source for the reporting solution must support incremental refreshes.
•The solution must report accurate data if an error occurs.
Issues
-
•A recent audit identified that all users can access the PII in the Planning Hub spreadsheet.
•After a developer deploys a change to the production environment, a user reports information is loaded incorrectly to the test system when processing a funding application.
•After deploying a change to the new eligibility assessment tool in the development environment, you observe that the changes do not appear in the development environment.
•After removing a column from the Planning Hub application and deploying the changes to the production environment, you observe that the column is still present.
•You deploy the customizations for the data model. Users report that the email address of the user who created the appointment is missing and that searches on the description information do not return any results.
You need to build the automation for the Planning Hub application.
Which connector should you use? To answer, move the appropriate connectors to the correct requirements. You may use each connector once, more than once, or not at all. You may need to move the split bar between panes or scroll to view content.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

Excel is commonly used as a data source for storing and retrieving structured information.

In Power Automate, this connector allows you to pull data from an Excel file stored in OneDrive or SharePoint.

Microsoft Teams is used for collaboration and approvals.

This connector facilitates automated approval workflows within Teams, where users can approve or reject submissions.

questions.examAnsDesc:
Web resource dependencies -
You can define dependencies between other web resources. The primary purpose of this feature is to allow association of String (RESX) web resources with the
JavaScript web resources that will use them. This is also the way that web resources required by HTML web resources for use offline can be configured to also be available offline.
Within a solution you can define dependencies within solution components. Up until Mode-driven Apps the main purpose of these dependencies was to prevent the deletion of a solution component when another solution component depended on it. With Model-driven apps the behavior for JavaScript web resources is enhanced so that any other web resource listed as a dependency to the JavaScript web resource will be loaded along with the JavaScript web resource.
Incorrect:
Not B: &ribbondebug=true is used for debugging.
Not C: When configuring ribbon elements, you can define specific rules to control when the ribbon elements are enabled.
Custom Rule uses the <CustomRule> element. Use this kind of rule to call a function in a Script (JScript) web resource that returns a Promise (Unified Interface) or boolean (Unified Interface and web client).

You are developing a model-driven app for a company.
When you create a new Account record, you must automatically display a form to collect data that is needed to create a Contact record. The form must switch to the appropriate form layout based on the contact type.
You open the Contact form by using JavaScript. You pass the contact type information to the form by using the Xrm.Navigation.openForm function. An OnLoad event handler in the Contact form processes the data and shows only the appropriate sections of the form for the given contact type.
You need to configure the receiving form to accept the data parameter.
Solution: In the form editor, add an event handler for the data parameter.
Does the solution meet the goal?
  • A. Yes
  • B. No
questions.examAnsDesc:
The solution meets the goal. Here's why:

The scenario requires passing data from one form (Account) to another (Contact) when opening the Contact form using JavaScript. The Xrm.Navigation.openForm function in Power Apps is specifically designed for this purpose. This function enables passing parameters to the target form.

To receive the data parameter passed via Xrm.Navigation.openForm, the target form (Contact form) needs to be configured to handle this incoming data. Adding an event handler to the Contact form's OnLoad event is the correct approach. Within this event handler, you can access the passed data and use it to modify the form's behavior, such as showing or hiding specific sections based on the contact type. This aligns precisely with the requirement of adapting the form layout based on the contact type. The data parameter is how you will receive the contact type from the initial form.

By adding the event handler to the "data" parameter in the Contact form editor, you're effectively enabling the form to receive and process the contact type information passed from the Account form. This ensures that the appropriate form sections are displayed based on the provided data.

Therefore, adding an event handler for the data parameter is the necessary step to receive and process data passed using Xrm.Navigation.openForm, making the solution correct.

Relevant links for further research:

  • Xrm.Navigation.openForm
  • Form Event Handlers in Power Apps

Background
-
Proseware, Inc. is an industry leading software company with several thousand employees. The company has had some trouble recruiting talented employees. Top-level candidates interview with the company but go on to work for competitors.
Feedback from candidates show that some offers were not accepted because the interview scheduling process was unpleasant. The company does not have a system to keep track of the candidates that were not selected.
Current Environment
-
The recruiting process starts when an individual applies for a position on the company website. The individual may have found the position on their own, they may have been officially referred by an employee, or in some cases were contacted directly by a hiring manager and encouraged to apply.
Recruiters schedule an interview with a hiring manager and interviews with two senior team members. Each interview results in feedback about the candidate and a recommendation whether to hire or not.
The recruiting team manages all information by using a model-driven application.
The company has the following Microsoft Dataverse tables and columns:
• JobPosting
- Hiring Manager - lookup to SystemUser
- Recruiter Assigned - lookup to SystemUser
• Contact (Job Applicant)
- Contact identifier
- First name
- Last name
- Time-Zone Offset
- Person of Interest - Yes/No (default)
• Application proapplication
- Contact identifier, Contact - lookup to Contact
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
- pro_recruiterassignedid
• Interview
- Application - lookup to Application
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
- Recommend - Choice (Yes (0), No (1), and null (default) are the available values)
- Person of Interest - Yes/No, No is the default value
• Referral
- Contact - lookup to Contact
- Referrer - lookup to SystemUser
- Job Posting - lookup to JobPosting
• SystemUser
- Manager - lookup to SystemUser
- Time-Zone Offset
• Recruiter
- Recruiter identifier
- Recruiter name
Applications
-
There may be multiple applications associated with each job posting. Applications are linked to an employee record if an employee referred the applicant for a position. The same individual can be an applicant for multiple job postings.
Interviews
-
Each interview is performed by an employee and is related to a single application.
The interview scheduling process may force potential candidates to accept interviews at unusual times with the senior team members due to time-zone differences.
Requirements. Interview Scheduling
The system must provide recruiters with a list of team members and their time-zone information. You must create a Microsoft Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) control for the Job Application form to display a list of senior team members who report directly to a hiring manager.
• The control must display the current time in each team member's local time.
• The control must be bound so that it minimizes the amount of code that must be written.
• You must display the list of team members and sort the list to show team members who reside in time zones closest to the applicant's time zone first.
You must develop a second PCF control that displays the time-zone name and current time on the Job Application form. You must display the data in the candidate’s local time.
Requirements. Historical Information Tracking
You must create a process to identify individuals as a person of interest that the company should consider hiring. You must assign each individual a score based on their past interactions.
• You must be able to determine the following information about a candidate:
- The number of interviews in the past two years and whether team members provided recommendations
- The number of hiring manager referrals and employee referrals in the past two years
- Whether the individual has any of the 12 designations or certifications that the company considers significant
• Only a single referral can be made per job application. The system must be able to support multiple referrals for a candidate.
• The system must track referrals even if an application is not completed.
Requirements. Historical Information Scoring
The automated process must run weekly to assess all candidates. The process must also run automatically when historical information is updated. You must be able to perform scoring by selecting a command button on the contact form.
• This new command button must only be visible to employees who belong to a security role assigned named Recruiter. The command button must not be visible to anyone unless the contact form is in Update mode.
• A person of interest is defined as having a score of 15 or more based on the following historical information criteria:
- Each interview with a recommendation adds two to the score.
- Each interview without a recommendation subtracts two from the score.
- Each employee or manager referral adds one to the score.
- Each designation or certification adds one to the score.
• All scoring elements must be recalculated when changes occur. You must assign the score to the Person of interest field.
• Values representing totals or scores must be stored in their own numeric fields.
• Plug-ins must be used to keep the Person of Interest field on active interview records associated with the Contact.
• Plug-ins registered on the update of the Person of interest field must send an email notification when the candidate named in the email is a person of interest. Recruiters must receive the message when the field is updated on the Contact record.
• Interviewers must get an email notification when the Person of Interest field on the interview record is successfully updated.
Requirements. Design Guidelines
The following design guidelines must be followed:
• Schema changes must be made using the method requiring the least amount of storage to meet the requirement.
• Out-of-the-box functionality must be used when possible.
• Any code required to calculate scores must be able to be run from a single point.
• Email notifications need to be kept to a minimum.
Issues
-
• Recruiters report that the command button to score a candidate is not working. You debug the code and observe that the context input parameter is null.
• The system does not support associating designations and certifications with candidates.
• The value for the field used by the PCF control to display local time is saved to Microsoft Dataverse each time an active application record is opened.
• Interviewers report that they do not receive email notifications when interview records are created for an existing person of interest.
You need to configure elements in the manifest for the PCF control used to display local time.
Which values should you use? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

Get the execution context. The function is passed an execution context as a parameter. This context is an object that contains all the information about the event that triggered the function (e.g., a field changing, a form loading). You need this context to access the next level of information.

Use getEventArgs() to get the column name. Within the execution context, the getEventArgs() method retrieves an object that provides details about the specific event. questions.examQue:
You develop a model-driven app in which client-side scripts are used extensively.
Users report that forms load quickly but become unresponsive.
You need to investigate the form issues before optimizing the forms.
What should you do first?

  • A. Use a Quick View form.
  • B. Add the URL parameter &ribbondebug=true.
  • C. Remove unused forms from the app.
  • D. Enable Offline mode.
  • E. Disable form event handlers.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Correct option: B – Add the URL parameter &ribbondebug=true.

  • Why it’s the best first step

    • Enabling ribbon debugging injects additional telemetry and error‑reporting into the form’s client‑side script execution.
    • It surfaces JavaScript console messages, script load failures, and performance bottlenecks that are otherwise hidden, allowing you to pinpoint the exact cause of the “unresponsive” behavior.
    • This approach is non‑intrusive; you can reproduce the issue with the debug flag on and gather actionable diagnostics before making any code changes.

  • Why the other options are less appropriate at this stage

    • A. Use a Quick View form – Quick Views are meant for lightweight data display, not for diagnosing script responsiveness; they do not provide any debugging insight.
    • C. Remove unused forms from the app – While reducing form count can improve overall app performance, it does not help isolate the specific script‑related problem on the affected form.
    • D. Enable Offline mode – Offline mode changes data caching behavior and is unrelated to client‑side script execution speed or responsiveness.
    • E. Disable form event handlers – Disabling handlers may mask the symptom but does not reveal why the scripts are unresponsive; it also risks losing critical functionality needed for diagnosis.

Bottom line: Activating ribbon debugging (&ribbondebug=true) is the precise, low‑impact technique to surface script errors and performance metrics, giving you the information needed to proceed with targeted optimizations.

questions.examAnsDesc:
If-None-Match: null

In Dataverse, an HTTP PATCH request behaves as an upsert operation by default. It will automatically update the record if it already exists or create it if it doesn't. Setting If-None-Match: null ensures that no conditional restrictions are placed on the request, allowing both inserts and updates to occur smoothly.

If-None-Match:

To restrict an upsert operation so that it only creates new records and never overwrites existing data, you must apply the If-None-Match: * header. If Dataverse detects that a record with the specified ID or alternate key already exists, the precondition fails, and it blocks the update by throwing an HTTP 412 Precondition Failed error.

questions.examAnsDesc:
Box 1: 0 0 4 * * 1-5 -
Azure Functions uses the NCronTab library to interpret NCRONTAB expressions.
An NCRONTAB expression is similar to a CRON expression except that it includes an additional sixth field at the beginning to use for time precision in seconds:
{second} {minute} {hour} {day} {month} {day-of-week}

NCRONTAB time zones -
The numbers in a CRON expression refer to a time and date, not a time span. For example, a 5 in the hour field refers to 5:00 AM, not every 5 hours.
The default time zone used with the CRON expressions is Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).
To have your CRON expression based on another time zone, create an app setting for your function app named WEBSITE_TIME_ZONE.

questions.examAnsDesc: Plug-in Profiler is not the best tool to use when debugging a plug-in that is not working as expected. The Plug-in Profiler is designed to troubleshoot performance issues with a plug-in by analyzing the execution of the plug-in on a remote server. It captures a profile of an executing plug-in and allows you to re-play the execution of the plug-in using Visual Studio on your local computer. However, it does not allow you to attach a debugger to the plug-in process and step through the code in real-time, which is typically necessary when debugging a plug-in. The Power Platform Tools for Visual Studio, on the other hand, is a tool that allows you to develop, debug, and deploy customizations for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform. It allows you to attach a debugger to the plug-in process, which allows you to step through the code and see what is happening at each stage of the validation process. This makes it more suitable for debugging the plug-in when the validation is not working as expected.

- Recruiter name

• The control must display the current time in each team member's local time.
• The control must be bound so that it minimizes the amount of code that must be written.
• You must display the list of team members and sort the list to show team members who reside in time zones closest to the applicant's time zone first.
You must develop a second PCF control that displays the time-zone name and current time on the Job Application form. You must display the data in the candidate’s local time.

You must create a process to identify individuals as a person of interest that the company should consider hiring. You must assign each individual a score based on their past interactions.

- The number of hiring manager referrals and employee referrals in the past two years

• A person of interest is defined as having a score of 15 or more based on the following historical information criteria:
- Each interview with a recommendation adds two to the score.
- Each interview without a recommendation subtracts two from the score.
- Each employee or manager referral adds one to the score.
- Each designation or certification adds one to the score.
• All scoring elements must be recalculated when changes occur. You must assign the score to the Person of interest field.
• Values representing totals or scores must be stored in their own numeric fields.

• Interviewers must get an email notification when the Person of Interest field on the interview record is successfully updated.

Background
-
Northwind Traders uses Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales to manage its sales process. To better understand its customers, Northwind Traders invests in a team of researchers who gather data from multiple sources. The company stores the data it collects in a Microsoft Azure SQL Database. The company plans to use the data to enrich account records and make the sales team more effective.
Current environment
-
Environment
-
•The company has three Microsoft Power Platform environments with Dynamics 365 Sales installed. The environments are named development, test, and production.
•Each environment has an application user that can be used for integrations.
•The company must use solutions to perform all customization and configuration deployment.
Data
-
•Researchers are responsible for creating account records.
•Researchers have permissions on the Account table to create records, read all records, and update records they own.
•A synchronous plug-in runs when an account record is created and could reassign the record to a different user.
•Users must access data as themselves to enforce security and audit changes.
•A column named new_dataid is added to the Account table. The column uniquely identifies which data it should receive.
•Researchers have researched only the top 20 percent of account records.
Web API
-
•The company creates an Azure Function to run a RESTful .NET Web API.
•Data can be retrieved by placing a GET request to the URL https://dataservice-[ENVIRONMENTNAME].azurewebsites.net/enrich/[DATAID].
•[ENVIRONMENTNAME] is the name of the Microsoft Power Platform environment that requests the data.
•[DATAID] is the new_dataid column in the Account table.
•The Web API response will return a 200 response plus data if the DataId is found. Otherwise, a 404 response is returned.
•Developers plan to create a custom connector from the Web API to make it accessible from Microsoft Power Platform.
Requirements
-
Custom connector
-
•The Web API definition used to create the custom connector must be generated based on a low-code technology.
•The URL used by the custom connector must incorporate the current environment name without hardcoding values.
•Errors generated by the custom connector must not cause downstream processes to fail.
•Text descriptions and field placeholder text that describe the use of the custom connector must appear for non-developers.
Process
-
•All account records must be updated with data from the Web API once automatically.
•Only account records that contain a DataId should be updated by the Web API.
•Researchers must create Power Automate flows to specify data analysis priority.
•The researchers require a process that repurposes a set of identical steps of parameterized Microsoft Dataverse queries from a Power Automate flow for use in other flows that have different parameters. The researchers want to avoid recreating the steps manually each time they create a flow to save time and avoid errors.
Issues
-
•A tester attempts to connect to the production instance of the Web API with a DataId that should return data. The tester receives an error stating that the remote name could not be resolved.
•A missing component causes an error to occur when importing the solution that contains the Power Automate flow to update account records in a test environment.

Background -
Northwind Traders uses Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales to manage its sales process. To better understand its customers, Northwind Traders invests in a team of researchers who gather data from multiple sources. The company stores the data it collects in a Microsoft Azure SQL Database. The company plans to use the data to enrich account records and make the sales team more effective.
Current environment -
Environment -
•The company has three Microsoft Power Platform environments with Dynamics 365 Sales installed. The environments are named development, test, and production.
•Each environment has an application user that can be used for integrations.
•The company must use solutions to perform all customization and configuration deployment.
Data -
•Researchers are responsible for creating account records.
•Researchers have permissions on the Account table to create records, read all records, and update records they own.
•A synchronous plug-in runs when an account record is created and could reassign the record to a different user.
•Users must access data as themselves to enforce security and audit changes.
•A column named new_dataid is added to the Account table. The column uniquely identifies which data it should receive.
•Researchers have researched only the top 20 percent of account records.
Web API -
•The company creates an Azure Function to run a RESTful .NET Web API.
•Data can be retrieved by placing a GET request to the URL https://dataservice-[ENVIRONMENTNAME].azurewebsites.net/enrich/[DATAID].
•[ENVIRONMENTNAME] is the name of the Microsoft Power Platform environment that requests the data.
•[DATAID] is the new_dataid column in the Account table.
•The Web API response will return a 200 response plus data if the DataId is found. Otherwise, a 404 response is returned.
•Developers plan to create a custom connector from the Web API to make it accessible from Microsoft Power Platform.

Custom connector -

•All account records must be updated with data from the Web API once automatically.

•Researchers must create Power Automate flows to specify data analysis priority.
•The researchers require a process that repurposes a set of identical steps of parameterized Microsoft Dataverse queries from a Power Automate flow for use in other flows that have different parameters. The researchers want to avoid recreating the steps manually each time they create a flow to save time and avoid errors.
Issues -
•A tester attempts to connect to the production instance of the Web API with a DataId that should return data. The tester receives an error stating that the remote name could not be resolved.
•A missing component causes an error to occur when importing the solution that contains the Power Automate flow to update account records in a test environment.
You need to determine the cause of the 404 error when connecting to the production instance of the Web API.
What do you identify?

  • A.The web service lacks data for the record.
  • B.An authentication error occurred.
  • C.The request timed-out.
  • D.The host name in the URL is missing a valid value.
questions.examAnsDesc: The error message indicating that the remote name could not be resolved suggests that the host name specified in the URL (https://dataservice-[ENVIRONMENTNAME].azurewebsites.net/enrich/[DATAID]) could not be resolved to a valid IP address, indicating a DNS resolution issue or a misconfiguration in the environment name specified in the URL. Therefore, the host name in the URL might be missing a valid value.

Background -
City Power & Light is an energy and utilities company that has offices in Europe. The company subsidizes home improvements for domestic customers, to improve energy efficiency and to meet environmental commitments. The company also distributes and generates electricity for domestic and commercial customers. The company has 2,000 employees in multiple offices and in work-from-home locations.
City Power & Light uses a team of schedulers, assessors, field engineers, and customer support agents for home improvements in a program named Get Energy Fit.
Current Environment -
Get Energy Fit Program -
City Power & Light uses the following to manage the Get Energy Fit program:
•The company uses a Microsoft Excel spreadsheet named Planning Hub on Microsoft SharePoint Online to store information about customer appointments, customer details, and customer eligibility in the program.
•The company records sensitive customer information that includes the document identification numbers and the customer's financial information.
•The company uses an assessor to verify customer eligibility in the program and to perform a suitability assessment. The assessor completes the suitability assessment by using a paper and clipboard at the customer property and enters the data to the Planning Hub after the assessment is completed. The assessor also uploads photographs to an on-premises document library. The assessor completes the eligibility assessment by using an application written in React.
•Schedulers use Microsoft Outlook to schedule engineers and assessors for home improvement appointments. About 200 appointments are scheduled daily.
•Employees for the company submit funding claims on behalf of the customer by uploading evidence and compliance checks information to an application named the Claim Submission Portal.
Technical Environment -
•Schedulers use Windows 11 desktop and laptop computers with the latest version of Microsoft Edge.
•Assessors use iOS and Android tablet devices.
•The Claim Submission Portal uses REST-based APIs for all operations and a dedicated testing environment. Authentication to the API is provided by using the following example header key and value pair: oAuthentication: 2C8D41431415E429C7FC7A74D8315
•The company uses Microsoft Azure for hosting multiple applications.
Requirements -
Overview -
City Power & Light plans to implement Microsoft Power Platform to improve the customer experience and increase delivery for the Get Energy Fit program.
Business Requirements -
•Only team leaders and senior managers should have access to read personally identifiable information (PII).
•All development changes must be tested in a separate environment.
•The company requires out-of-the-box solutions, when possible.
•Sensitive credentials, such as user passwords and API secrets, must be stored securely.
•The Claim Submission Portal must allow citizen developers to create automated solutions.
•Customer and appointment information must be accessible to all applications.
Planning Hub Application -
The company is planning to replace the Planning Hub spreadsheet with a new application. The new application has the following requirements:
•The application must support a component design that provides rapid changes requested by the schedulers.
•The data model for the application must capture the following information:
oInformation about customers such as name, address, and other PII. oThe data and time for an assessor's or engineer's appointment. Schedulers must be able to view all appointments without filters. oRecords the details of the home improvements installed for the customer. oContains all the information and evidence for submission to the Claim Submission Portal.
•After an assessor uploads the funding application and all evidence after a home improvement has been complete, the company requires that the status of the application is set to Submit and should run the following:
oRetrieve the details about the customer and the improvement installed. oSend an approval to a senior manager to review and approve in Microsoft Teams. oUpload the information to the API endpoint. oIf the upload fails to complete, it should retry after a delay of 30 seconds up to three times. If an error occurs after three times, the application should send an email notification to the application support team. oMust record the status on the funding application.
Suitability Assessment Tool -
The company plans to implement a new application named the Suitability Assessment Tool for the assessors. The new application has the following requirements:
•Must integrate with Microsoft Power Platform.
•Assessors must be able to complete the eligibility assessment by using the Suitability Assessment Tool. The assessors must be able to upload photographs to the on-premises file share.
•Must be developed by using modular components that can be used by other applications.
•Must be optimized for use on tablet devices.
•All changes to the application must be completed in the Suitability Assessment Tool solution.
Reporting -
The company has the following requirements for a reporting solution:
•The data source for the reporting solution must support incremental refreshes.
•The solution must report accurate data if an error occurs.
Issues -
•A recent audit identified that all users can access the PII in the Planning Hub spreadsheet.
•After a developer deploys a change to the production environment, a user reports information is loaded incorrectly to the test system when processing a funding application.
•After deploying a change to the new eligibility assessment tool in the development environment, you observe that the changes do not appear in the development environment.
•After removing a column from the Planning Hub application and deploying the changes to the production environment, you observe that the column is still present.
•You deploy the customizations for the data model. Users report that the email address of the user who created the appointment is missing and that searches on the description information do not return any results.
You need to resolve the issue with the eligibility assessment tool.
Which two commands should you run? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

  • A.pac solution version
  • B.pac solution import
  • C.pac pcf push
  • D.pac pcf version --strategy manifest
questions.examAnsDesc:
pac solution version: This command is used to manage the version of your solution. It helps ensure that the solution is correctly versioned, which is crucial for tracking changes and ensuring compatibility.

pac pcf version --strategy manifest: This command is used to update the version of Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) controls within your solution. The --strategy manifest option ensures that the version is updated based on the manifest file, which is important for maintaining consistency and resolving version-related issues.

questions.examQue:
A company requires a plug-in that makes multiple requests to an external web service. The plug-in must not time out when the web service has issues or is slow to respond.
You need to create the plug-in.
What should you do?

  • A.Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
  • B.Set the HTTP connection KeepAlive property to false.
  • C.Register the plug-in by using isolation mode = none.
  • D.Assign the IOrganizationService object to a member variable.
questions.examAnsDesc:
A is correct because registering the plug-in to run synchronously ensures that all operations complete before returning control to the caller, thus preventing timeouts during external service calls.

Reasoning:

When a plug-in is registered to execute synchronously, it runs in the same thread context as the operation triggering it, allowing for real-time processing of the tasks, including making multiple web service calls. This is crucial for ensuring that the required actions are completed sequentially and that no premature termination occurs due to timeouts associated with asynchronous processing. Real-time interaction with web services necessitates robust error handling to manage responses effectively, improving the reliability of the application.

Evaluation of Other Options:

  • B. Set the HTTP connection KeepAlive property to false: Setting KeepAlive to false may optimize certain requests, but it does not directly influence the handling of multiple requests or mitigate timeouts. In scenarios of slow response from the service, this setting could lead to increased latency due to the overhead of establishing new connections for each request.

  • C. Register the plug-in by using isolation mode = none: Using isolation mode level "none" allows the plug-in to run in the same process as the calling assembly but may expose it to more risks and potential failure points. This mode can lead to issues if the external service fails, impacting the stability of the main process and increasing the likelihood of timeouts, rather than addressing the core issue of handling external calls effectively.

  • D. Assign the IOrganizationService object to a member variable: While this may help optimize service calls by reusing the service instance, it doesn’t specifically address the timeout scenario or the handling of slow external requests. The plug-in would still ultimately fail if the external service is unresponsive, regardless of how the service object is managed.

References:
  1. Microsoft Docs - Register a plug-in
  2. Microsoft Docs - Plug-in and Custom Workflow Activity Registration Tool
  3. Microsoft Docs - Performance considerations and best practices

questions.examQue:
A company requires a plug-in that makes multiple requests to an external web service. The plug-in must not time out when the web service has issues or is slow to respond.
You need to create the plug-in.
What should you do?

  • A.Register the plug-in to run synchronously.
  • B.Register the plug-in by using isolation mode = none.
  • C.Set the HTTP connection timeout value explicitly to limit how long each connection can remain open.
  • D.Register the plug-in step once for each web service request.
questions.examAnsDesc:
C is correct because setting the HTTP connection timeout value explicitly allows for better control over the duration of external web service requests, thereby preventing timeouts during slow responses.

In the context of plug-ins in the Microsoft Power Platform, managing external web service calls is critical for ensuring smooth operational flows. By configuring the HTTP connection timeout, a developer can specify how long the system should wait for a response before it considers the connection failed. This is particularly beneficial when external services are unreliable or slow, as it allows the application to remain responsive rather than timing out abruptly, which can lead to incomplete operations.

Critical Evaluation of Incorrect Options:

  • A. Register the plug-in to run synchronously. This approach would lead to a synchronous operation that blocks the execution thread until the service responds. If the external service is slow or unresponsive, this can cause significant delays or timeouts in the overall process, defeating the purpose of robustness against slow responses.

  • B. Register the plug-in by using isolation mode = none. Isolation mode = none runs the plug-in in the same process as the calling code, which can cause stability issues. If the external web service hangs or crashes, it could also crash the entire application, making it unsuitable for handling unreliable services.

  • D. Register the plug-in step once for each web service request. This approach would unnecessarily complicate the registration process and increase maintenance overhead. It does not enhance the robustness of handling slow responses, as each registered instance would still suffer from the same timeout limitations as a single request.

By opting for option C, a developer ensures that the plug-in maintains high responsiveness and resilience against external service latencies, facilitating overall application stability and user experience.

References:

  • https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powerapps/developer/data-platform/plugins
  • https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powerapps/developer/data-platform/web-service-requests
  • https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powerapps/developer/data-platform/plug-ins-isolation-modes

questions.examQue:
You are creating a canvas app that will create rows in a Dataverse table.
When a row is created, additional business logic must be performed on a related row. A cloud flow triggered by the canvas app must perform the business logic.
You need to create the cloud flow.
Which trigger should you use?

  • A. Dataverse - When an action is performed
  • B. Manually trigger a flow
  • C. Dataverse - When a row is added
  • D. Power Apps (V2)
questions.examAnsDesc:
The correct trigger for the cloud flow is C. Dataverse - When a row is added.

Here's why: The canvas app creates rows in a Dataverse table. The core requirement is that when a new row is created, additional business logic must be executed on a related row. The "Dataverse - When a row is added" trigger is specifically designed to fire automatically whenever a new row is inserted into the specified Dataverse table. This aligns directly with the scenario's need to react to row creation events.

Option A, "Dataverse - When an action is performed," requires a specific action to be called which isn't the intent here, as the trigger should simply react to row creation.

Option B, "Manually trigger a flow," requires manual initiation, contradicting the automatic execution requirement following row creation in the canvas app. This option would not provide the automatic response that is necessary for this scenario.

Option D, "Power Apps (V2)," is suitable when the cloud flow needs to be initiated from within the Power App and passed information from the app. While the app is involved in the broader process, it is the row creation event in Dataverse that should trigger the business logic, not the Power App directly. The Power Apps (V2) trigger is designed primarily to accept input from the Power App, which is not required in this scenario - we only want to respond to the new row creation.

Therefore, the "Dataverse - When a row is added" trigger is the most appropriate choice because it directly addresses the scenario's need for automated execution of business logic based on the creation of a new row in a Dataverse table. It's an event-driven approach that simplifies the workflow and ensures that the logic executes immediately after a new row is added without requiring manual intervention or action calls.

For further reading on Power Automate triggers, particularly those involving Dataverse, refer to these resources:

  • Use triggers to start a cloud flow
  • Dataverse connector - Triggers

questions.examQue:
You have a Power Automate flow. The flow uses an HTTP action to connect to a web service and update a Microsoft Dataverse record with the result.
You must modify the flow to send an email if the web service connection fails.
You need to update the flow.
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. Choose two.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

  • A. Configure the send email step to run when the previous step fails.
  • B. Add a send email step after the update Dataverse record step.
  • C. Add a send email step after the HTTP step.
  • D. Update the HTTP step settings and set the retry policy to: None.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Technical justification (exam‑style)

  • Option A – Configure the Send Email step to run when the previous step fails
    Sets the Run‑after condition to “has failed”. This explicitly tells the flow to execute the email action only when the preceding HTTP activity throws an error, which is exactly the requirement (notify on connection failure).

  • Option C – Add a Send Email step after the HTTP step
    Places the email action in the flow sequence immediately downstream of the HTTP call. Because the email step follows the HTTP step, it can be triggered by the failure condition defined in A. The order is important: the email must be evaluated after the HTTP action so that its execution context reflects the success/failure of that call.

  • Why the other options are unsuitable

    • B – Add a Send Email step after the Update Dataverse record step – This would cause the email to fire only when the record‑update step fails, not when the HTTP call fails. The failure point is mis‑aligned with the requirement.
    • D – Update the HTTP step settings and set the retry policy to: None – Changing the retry policy does not provide any notification mechanism; it merely controls how retries are attempted. It does not trigger an email on failure.

Conclusion – The combination of A (defining the failure‑triggered run‑after condition) and C (positioning the email action right after the HTTP step) correctly implements the needed error‑notification logic in the Power Automate flow.

You are an integration that sends created records from a custom Dataverse table to an exposed REST API.
When the REST API is unavailable, you must be able to retry if the response status code is 500.
You need to select a solution that meets the requirement.
Solution: Register a webhook by using the REST API as the endpoint. Wait for the webhook to automatically retry when a failure occurs.
Does the solution meet the goal?

  • A. Yes
  • B. No
questions.examAnsDesc:
Answer: B – No

  • Registering a webhook only creates the subscription; the platform does not automatically retry on HTTP 500 responses.
  • Webhook retry behavior is limited to transient connectivity failures (e.g., network timeouts) and is not configurable for specific status codes such as 500.
  • To meet the requirement you must implement explicit retry logic (e.g., exponential back‑off) that inspects the response status and retries only when the code is 500.
  • Therefore the proposed solution does not satisfy the “retry on 500” condition, making option B the correct choice.

(Alternative approaches such as using Azure Logic Apps, Azure Functions, or a custom connector with built‑in retry policies would be appropriate.)

questions.examAnsDesc:

  • Why: This trigger is used when an automation needs to run instantly based on an explicit user action (like clicking a button in a canvas app, a mobile app, or inputting on-demand data). It allows the flow to accept input parameters directly from the user at the exact moment of execution.


2. Record ID to update: From the trigger

  • Why: When using an instant or manual trigger, any record context or unique identifiers (IDs) captured during the initiation phase are exposed as dynamic content outputs immediately under the trigger block. Selecting From the trigger ensures the flow passes that exact identifier downstream to a Dataverse "Update a row" action without needing extra query steps or variables.

questions.examQue:
You write a plug-in that creates a row in a custom table.
Only some users have permission to create rows in the custom table.
You need to allow the plug-in to run for all users by using the principle of least privilege.
What should you do?

  • A. Initiate the iOrganizationService by passing the ID of a user with permissions to create rows in the custom table.
  • B. Ensure all users have been granted the Environment Maker role.
  • C. Set Run in the User’s Context to Calling User in the plug-in step.
  • D. Ensure all users have the Acton Behalf of Another User permission assigned to one of their security roles.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Why option A is correct

  • The plug‑in must execute under an account that actually possesses the Create privilege on the custom table.
  • By initializing IOrganizationService with the GUID of a user (or a service account) that already has that permission, the plug‑in runs with the minimum set of rights required – only that user can create rows, and the plug‑in inherits those rights.
  • This satisfies the principle of least privilege: the plug‑in does not grant every user full access; instead it relies on a dedicated privileged identity to perform the privileged operation on behalf of the caller.

Why the other options are unsuitable

  • B – Environment Maker role – This role is intended for environment‑level customizations, not for granting table‑level write permissions. Granting it to all users would give them broad admin capabilities, violating least‑privilege and creating security over‑reach.

  • C – Run in the User’s Context (Calling User) – When a plug‑in runs in the calling user’s context, it inherits that user’s security rights. Since most users lack the Create privilege on the custom table, the plug‑in would fail for them; the approach does not provide the needed privilege.

  • D – “Act on Behalf Of Another User” permission – This permission is used for impersonation scenarios (e.g., when a user explicitly chooses to act on behalf of another). It does not automatically grant the ability to create rows, nor does it ensure the plug‑in runs with the required rights for all callers.

Implementation tip 

using Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk;var service = new OrganizationService(Guid.Parse("UserIdWithCreatePermission"));Entity newRecord = new Entity("new_customtable");newRecord["new_name"] = "Sample";service.Create(newRecord);

By passing the GUID of a user (or a dedicated service account) that holds the Create right on the custom table, the plug‑in can create rows for any caller while still adhering to least‑privilege principles.

questions.examQue:
You have a model-driven app form that uses Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord during the OnSave event to update a related record.
You observe during testing that the related record does not always update when it should.
You need to ensure that the current record is saved and the related record is updated consistently.
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. Choose two.
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

  • A. Add logic before the update to ensure that the request is made only when the value has changed.
  • B. Enable the Async OnSave app setting.
  • C. Wrap the update in a promise.
  • D. Add executionContext.getEventArgs[].disableAsyncTimeout[] before the update.
  • E. Add executionContext.getEventArgs[].preventDefault[] before the update.
questions.examAnsDesc:
Why B and C are the correct choices

  • B – Enable the Async OnSave app setting

    • When this setting is turned on, the OnSave event runs asynchronously, giving the platform enough time to complete the Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord call without aborting the form save.
    • Asynchronous execution prevents the “record not saved” race condition that occurs when the update is forced synchronously during the save transaction.

  • C – Wrap the update in a promise

    • Returning a promise from the OnSave handler tells the framework that the operation is asynchronous and that the save should wait until the promise resolves.
    • This guarantees that the related record is successfully updated before the current record’s save completes, ensuring consistent state across both records.

Why the other options are not appropriate

  • A – Add logic to fire only when the value has changed

    • While this reduces unnecessary calls, it does not address the underlying timing issue that causes the related record to be missed; the problem is not about unnecessary calls but about reliable completion of the async update.

  • D – Add executionContext.getEventArgs[].disableAsyncTimeout[]

    • This method does not exist in the XRM SDK; attempting to use it would cause a runtime error and cannot influence the async timeout behavior.

  • E – Add executionContext.getEventArgs[].preventDefault[]

    • preventDefault is not a supported API for the OnSave event and would have no effect on the asynchronous update; it is unrelated to ensuring the related record is saved.

Conclusion
Enabling the Async OnSave setting (B) and properly handling the asynchronous operation with a promise (C) together guarantee that the current record is saved and the related record is updated reliably and consistently. The other options either do not solve the timing problem or are not valid APIs.

HOTSPOT
